conventions.sigma: 1-sigma. sigma_3 is repeated for readability only; the generator reads sigma.

conventions.lognormal: param = TT * exp(sigma_log * Z), sigma_log = ln(1 + sigma)

TOX_50.note: ONC25 sets the gate oxide by the GATE rating, not the drain rating (its 200 V LDMOS with a 5 V gate uses the 13 nm oxide). All 13 AutoHV VDMOS are rated 5.5 V DC on the gate, so all of them sit on this oxide. VDMOS cards carry no tox parameter, so the loading reaches them through KP/VTO.

vdmos_loading.mechanism: see dependent_parameters: VTO_<vdmos>_STAT follows TOX_50, and k1/vth0 follow TOX_<class>
vdmos_loading.why_not_here: This entry previously duplicated the coupling as applies_to 'via-loading' on KP_*_STAT and VTO_*_STAT. Ruling 1.2 gave the coupling measured per-card coefficients (analytic - bsim3_residual), which live in dependent_parameters. Two live mechanisms for one effect would let the generator apply it twice, so dependent_parameters is authoritative and this is a pointer.

_RDSW_template._comment: one entry per MOS/VDMOS device; VDMOS applies to both rd and rs, which come from the same drift module

DL_POLY.note: Acts on MOS channel length and on the drawn WIDTH of a poly resistor (the CD controls the drawn poly edge in both cases).

RSH_GATE.note: A separate layer from RPOLY_HI/LO. This PDK declares no gate-poly sheet resistance; ruling Q-B introduces it for the rgate term only.

_RHEAD_template.note: ONC25 carries only a contact-head temperature coefficient, no ohm-per-contact value (checked per ruling F7), so nominal and sigma are declared: silicided 5-10 ohm/contact.

_CPER_template._comment: one entry per capacitor type; new term, see wrapper section 5.4
_CPER_template.constraint: CDEN and CPER are split so total C is unchanged at each type's regression-golden geometry (ruling Q-C).

_VBE_template._comment: physical variable for BJT global spread; IS is derived from it (ruling 3.1)
_VBE_template.derivation: IS = IS_TT * exp(-dVbe / V_T), V_T = kT/q at 27 C

_RPAR_template._comment: BJT parasitic series resistances rb/rc/re move together (one module)

_VF_template._comment: physical variable for diode global spread; IS derived (ruling 3.1)

_BV_template._comment: one entry per VDMOS; drift doping sets breakdown

JS_MOS.note: Ruling 3.4: js follows IS-style junction variation at 20 % 3-sigma.

_VTH_inputs.Q_f_source: literature: thermal oxide on (100) Si, standard texts (Nicollian & Brews; Sze)
_VTH_inputs.Q_f_variation_note: The ruling's prose states 50 % and its expected-totals table is reproduced by 30 %. 50 % is used per the autonomy-rule tie-break (closer to current PDK behaviour); the 30 % totals are in the handoff.
_VTH_inputs.Q_dep_source: literature: typical Vth-implant control budget for 0.18-0.25 um
_VTH_inputs.Q_dep_note: effective channel charge, not dose alone: implant energy/profile and anneal thermal budget move the depletion charge that sets Vth, and the fab control budget is on the resulting charge
_VTH_inputs.poly_depletion: held at zero: second order at these oxide thicknesses

_sharing.rule: Variables sharing a physical cause share ONE draw with coefficient 1.0; everything else is independent. No rho decomposition: the declared rho was the least-grounded number in the model and nothing consumed it.
_sharing.consequence: Corner distance is the Euclidean norm of z, which is what build_corners.py computes and what corner_construction states.

_U0_declared._comment: Ruling U2. U0_<device> is DECLARED, not solved. The per-class Idsat bands it used to be solved against were externally sourced, and the 14 % LDMOS band was invented; both are retired. Each device's Idsat sigma is now whatever its own grounded inputs predict, reported as metric_3sigma_swing.
_U0_declared.source: literature: mobility spread for a 0.18-0.25 um BCD flow
_U0_declared.supersedes: _U0_calibration, whose class_bands_3sigma {18: 0.20, 33: 0.20, 50: 0.14, 12: 0.14, vdmos: 0.14} came from an external Idsat FF/SS table and whose LDMOS entry was invented.
_U0_declared.anti_correlation: U2 also adopts the U0/Rd anti-correlation as a structural feature, carried by sign rather than by a solved VDMOS calibration.
_U0_declared.sigma_zero_criterion: d ln(Id)/d ln(U0) on the device's own classic bench, below 0.4. Where the drift region dominates the current, mobility has no meaningful lever and a non-zero sigma(KP) would describe the model rather than the device.
_U0_declared.independence_note: U0 and RD are INDEPENDENT draws. Channel mobility is set by the body implant and drift resistance by the drift implant -- separate process steps, so independent draws are the default under the identity rule. A shared signed draw (one variable moving KP up and RD down together) is a legitimate alternative structure used by some libraries; it is not adopted here for lack of a physical basis in AutoHV's declared flow. Note this is a statement about the PROCESS, not about the corner direction: the fast direction moves both because both raise current, which is a property of the direction, not a correlation.

vsat.held_at_TT: no corner or spread data in ONC25; second-order at the corner biases used here

pclm.held_at_TT: no corner or spread data; affects output conductance, not the corner metric

eta0.held_at_TT: DIBL is fitted per card; no independent spread source

cj.reason: junction depth and implant dose move together; declared weak coupling per ruling 3.4

tf.held_at_TT: BJT transit time; no corner data, fT is second-order for the corner metric

BVCBO.reason: same avalanche physics as the VDMOS breakdown term

vth0.reason: Ruling AB1 S2.1: the oxide contribution to Vth is NOT in the private VTH_<device> draw. It enters through the shared TOX_<class> draw so that same-oxide devices correlate in Monte Carlo. Thicker oxide -> higher |Vth|.

validation.method: tox perturbed +-1.33 % (the TOX_* 1-sigma); Vth read from the model itself (@m.xm1.m0[vth]) with no extraction criterion, at each group's own classic bench (sizing-guide W, L = Lmin_fab), after the k3 grounding landed
validation.bsim3_residual_is_negative: On every card |Vth| FALLS as tox rises at bench geometry. An L-sweep on NMOS50 (W 4.7 um) shows why: as carded the residual is -1.171 mV at L = 0.5 um, -0.222 at 1 um, then +0.035..+0.049 at L >= 2 um; with dvt0/dvt1/dvt2/k3 zeroed it collapses to ~0 at every length. So BSIM3's implicit tox dependence is entirely the short-channel and narrow-width terms, which dominate and reverse the trend at bench lengths. applied = analytic - (negative) is therefore 10-22 % LARGER than analytic.
validation.supersedes: The earlier decision to apply the full closed form, and the 3.7-19.5 % residual reported at Stop A'. That figure came from constant-current and gm-max extraction, both of which move with tox themselves and gave criterion-dependent, sign-unstable results (NMOS18 read -0.18 mV at a 1x W/L criterion, -0.61 at 0.1x, +3.52 at 10x).

k1.reason: Ruling AB1 S2.1: gamma scales with oxide thickness, so d k1 / k1 = d tox / tox.
k1.validation: showmod confirms BSIM3 does not scale k1 with tox at all: k1 reads back 0.68 unchanged at tox 4.25 and 4.307 nm. The residual is exactly 0, so the generator applies the full relative coupling d k1 / k1 = d tox / tox.

VTO_<vdmos>_STAT.reason: Ruling AB1 S2.1: all thirteen VDMOS sit on the 5 V oxide; k1_equiv comes from the 11 nm body-doping derivation (docs/stat-model.md S1.2).

local_mismatch._convention: 1-sigma Pelgrom coefficients, foundry units. sigma = A / sqrt(W*L*M) for MOS, A / sqrt(area*M) for BJT/diode, per the wrapper forms.

_A_VT_derivation.expression: A_VT(RDF) = (q/Cox)*sqrt(Na*Wdep/3), with Na = (k1*Cox)^2/(2*q*eps_si) taken from the card's own k1 and Wdep = sqrt(4*eps_si*phi_F/(q*Na)) self-consistent; the total is A_VT = A_VT(RDF)/sqrt(f_RDF). Substituting Na(k1) collapses the whole expression to c_RDF*sqrt(tox*k1), so c_RDF is computed, never fitted.
_A_VT_derivation.f_RDF_basis: Random dopant fluctuation carries roughly half of sigma(Vth) at the 0.18-0.25 um node, i.e. ~0.25-0.35 of the variance; 0.30 is taken. The ~0.65 share quoted for advanced nodes applies at <=45 nm. Oxide charge, line-edge roughness and halo/implant non-uniformity carry the remainder.
_A_VT_derivation.validation: c_RDF is constant to 3.18 % (2.1661..2.2361) across tox 4.25-31 nm and Na 9.0e16-7.9e17 cm-3. A wrong doping exponent would drift c systematically with tox; it does not, which is the evidence for the tox*Na^(1/4) shape.
_A_VT_derivation.retired: Supersedes the 'A_VT ~ 1 mV.um per nm of tox (+-50 %)' thin-oxide heuristic previously used as the target band, and the externally anchored ladder that preceded it.
citations: Stolk, Widdershoven & Klaassen, IEEE TED 45(9), 1998 -- RDF model for sigma(Vth)
Asenov, IEEE TED 45(12), 1998 -- statistical 3-D simulation of random dopant effects
Mizuno, Okamura & Toriumi, IEEE TED 41(11), 1994 -- measured dopant-fluctuation Vth spread
Kuhn et al., IEEE TED 58(8), 2011 -- process-variation sources by node (the ~65 % RDF share is a <=45 nm figure)
_A_VT_derivation.least_checked: The 12 V (31 nm) rung is the least externally checked: no 12 V-class comparison exists, and the 31 nm end is where an oxide-charge term would matter most.

A_VT.convention: sigma(Vth) at the W_REF = 10 um reference cell, WIDTH-normalised: the wrapper computes AGAUSS(0, coef, 3)/sqrt(mtot) with mtot = (W/W_REF)*M. This is NOT an area-normalised Pelgrom coefficient and must not be converted into one -- see docs/stat-model.md S3.2.
A_VT.source: declared (phase-3, per-class; heavier body doping and drift-field Vth sensitivity rising with class)
A_VT.note: The per-class dependence is deliberate and is retained. A Pelgrom form c_RDF*sqrt(tox*k1_equiv) was derived at the 11 nm oxide and gives a nearly flat 6.43-7.20 mV.um, which would erase that dependence and is in the wrong normalisation besides; it is not used. Any comparison against an external coefficient lives only in the local plausibility script as pass/fail.

_RESISTORS._comment: the single lumped coefficient is split into four terms, constrained at the 10x10 um reference geometry (ruling Q-C / brief 5.3)
_RESISTORS.split_constraint: at the passives_mc local-mismatch reference geometry (W=L=10 um, NS=1, M=1) the combined sigma equals today's per-type lumped value exactly; end+head carry <= 20 % of the variance there. Note this is a different geometry from the R(V) goldens (100x10 um).
_RESISTORS.note: Ruling F1: grounded on ONC25's model-form Pelgrom coefficient (1.1-1.55 %.um), which is consistent with today's 1.06. The spec-table column is NOT used; see the discrepancy note in docs/stat-model.md.

A_C.note: ONC25 is silent on MIM matching.

A_CPER.note: New perimeter term; value set by the Q-C constraint, which holds total C at each type's golden geometry of 100x100 um.

A_VBE.note: Reproduces today's 0.15 mV pair sigma at AREA=1, so not a value change. Literature for BCD vertical NPNs is 0.3-1 mV.um, so the value sits at the top of that band.

_BJT.area_convention: sigma = A / sqrt(AREA * 100 * M) um^2; AREA is a multiple of the declared 100 um^2 cell, so AREA=0.04 is 4 um^2 (ruling Q-E)

benches._comment: Reference bench per group, taken from docs/sizing-guide.json rather than invented. classic = the corner direction bench (ruling F8); analog = the gm/Id ~ 6 mirror point, reported alongside.
benches._mos_classic: Vgs = Vds = class supply, L = sizing-guide analog default, W = the 10 uA mirror-point width
benches._mos_analog: the sizing-guide 10 uA mirror point (W, Vgs, gm/Id ~ 6), Vds = supply/2

_resistors.layer_ref: RPOLY_HI 2 um width, per the sizing guide's precision default
_resistors.golden_geometry: the resistor C(V)/R(V) goldens use 100x10 um (10 squares); the direction bench uses the sizing guide's precision default (RPOLY_HI, 2 um width)

_capacitors.geometry: each type's regression-golden geometry: 100x100 um (10000 um^2), which is what pdk_validation/regression/run_passives.py generates the C(V) goldens at

corner_construction.method: Q-A ruling: measured worst-case direction, not hand-declared loadings
steps: 2. Measure g_i = d ln(metric)/d z_i for every variable the group depends on, on its classic bench.
3. z_fast = 3 * g / |g|; z_slow = -z_fast. Mahalanobis length is exactly 3 by construction.
4. Record bench, bias, and the g vector (classic and analog) in corners.json.
corner_construction.shared_variable_rule: When several selected groups pull a shared variable the same way, the preset generator takes the normalized sum of directions and rescales to the preset's declared distance. Conflicts are reported in corners.json; last-listed group wins only in case = -1 manual mode.
corner_construction.SPD_note: SPD_<group> is a derived direction, not a sampled variable. Monte Carlo samples the independent variables; SPD exists only to define corners.

model_parameter_changes._comment: Non-statistical model-card values changed by this program. The generator writes these into every BSIM3 card; brief section 0 requires physics, source and before/after for each.

k3.evidence: docs/bsim3-defaults-audit.md: at W=0.4 um the default raises Vth +238 mV vs a 50 um device (+29 mV once grounded); Id/W 111.9 -> 125.5 uA/um
